description: Adversaries can steal application access tokens as a means of acquiring credentials to access remote systems and resources. Application access tokens are used to make authorized API requests on behalf of a user or service and are commonly used as a way to access resources in cloud and container-based applications and software-as-a-service (SaaS). OAuth is one commonly implemented framework that issues tokens to users for access to systems. Adversaries who steal account API tokens in cloud and containerized environments may be able to access data and perform actions with the permissions of these accounts.

falco.trigger_condition: Unusual API calls made with existing OAuth tokens from unexpected source IPs or at unusual times. In a containerized context, reads of mounted service account token files (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token) would be a Falco file access detection signal.

mitigation: Implement short-lived OAuth tokens with strict expiry. Use token binding to prevent token replay from different clients. Monitor for token use from unexpected geographic locations or IP addresses. Apply least-privilege scoping to all issued tokens.
